beats.title: Hollerith Tabulator Tallies Census
beats.description: Punched cards fed an electric tabulating machine that tallied a national population count far faster than hand counting.

beats.title: De Forest Invents the Triode Tube
beats.description: A three-element vacuum tube could amplify and switch signals, becoming the basic building block of early electronic computers.

beats.title: Eccles-Jordan Flip-Flop Circuit
beats.description: Two vacuum tubes wired to hold one of two stable states gave electronics its first memory cell, the root of every register.

beats.title: Bush's Differential Analyzer Runs
beats.description: A room-sized analog machine at MIT solved complex differential equations using rotating shafts and gears.

beats.title: Zuse Completes the Z1
beats.description: A German engineer built a binary, programmable machine in his parents' living room, using mechanical memory and logic.

beats.title: Zuse's Z3 Computes
beats.description: The first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer ran on telephone relays in Berlin.

beats.title: ENIAC Is Unveiled
beats.description: A Pennsylvania team revealed a giant electronic computer with thousands of vacuum tubes, hailed as an electronic brain.

beats.title: Transistor Invented at Bell Labs
beats.description: Researchers made a tiny solid-state amplifier from germanium that would replace bulky vacuum tubes in all electronics.

beats.title: Manchester Baby Runs a Program
beats.description: A small English machine became the first computer to run a program stored in its own electronic memory.

beats.title: UNIVAC I Delivered
beats.description: The first commercial computer made in America went to the Census Bureau, later famous for predicting an election result on TV.

beats.title: TRADIC Transistor Computer Built
beats.description: Bell Labs finished a military machine with hundreds of transistors in place of vacuum tubes, small enough to fit in a bomber.

beats.title: IBM Unveils the Hard Disk Drive
beats.description: A refrigerator-sized cabinet of spinning platters stored millions of characters and let data be reached at random.

beats.title: First Integrated Circuit Built
beats.description: An engineer at Texas Instruments made a working circuit with several components on one piece of semiconductor.

beats.title: DEC Delivers the PDP-1
beats.description: An interactive computer, sold for a fraction of a mainframe's price, launched the minicomputer and early video games.

beats.title: IBM Announces System/360
beats.description: A family of compatible mainframes let customers upgrade without rewriting software, defining big business computing.

beats.title: DEC Launches the PDP-8
beats.description: A cheap, compact minicomputer put real computing power into labs and small firms for a fraction of a mainframe's cost.

beats.title: Intel's 4004 Microprocessor Debuts
beats.description: A whole central processor on a single fingernail-sized chip began the microprocessor revolution.

beats.title: Xerox Alto Computer Built
beats.description: A research machine combined a mouse, windows and a bitmapped display, previewing the personal computers to come.

beats.title: Altair 8800 Kit Computer Appears
beats.description: A hobbyist kit advertised on a magazine cover inspired a generation of garage builders and young software founders.

beats.title: Cray-1 Supercomputer Installed
beats.description: A C-shaped machine with a ring of bench seating went into a New Mexico weapons lab and became the iconic supercomputer.

beats.title: Apple II Goes on Sale
beats.description: A ready-to-use home computer with colour graphics and a keyboard brought computing to ordinary homes and schools.

beats.title: IBM PC Launched
beats.description: The computing giant entered the desktop market with an open design that set the standard for decades of business PCs.

beats.title: Apple Macintosh Debuts
beats.description: A compact beige computer with a mouse and on-screen icons made the graphical interface familiar to mainstream buyers.

beats.title: ARM1 Processor First Runs
beats.description: A small British team's simple, power-frugal processor worked first time, seeding the chips later found in most phones.

beats.title: Intel 486 Chip Debuts
beats.description: A processor became the first of its family to pack over a million transistors, powering a generation of desktop PCs.

beats.title: Intel Ships the Pentium
beats.description: Intel's new processor, named rather than numbered, brought a major speed boost and a very public arithmetic bug scandal.

beats.title: Deep Blue Beats Kasparov
beats.description: An IBM supercomputer won a six-game match against the reigning world chess champion, stunning the public.

beats.title: Apple Launches the Original iMac
beats.description: A translucent, colourful all-in-one desktop with no floppy drive made the home computer a fashion object.

beats.title: Nvidia Brands the First GPU
beats.description: The GeForce 256 moved graphics calculations onto a dedicated chip, later repurposed for scientific computing and AI.

beats.title: IBM Quantum Computer Factors 15
beats.description: A seven-qubit quantum computer ran a famous factoring algorithm, an early demonstration of quantum hardware doing real work.

beats.title: AMD Opteron Brings 64-Bit to x86
beats.description: A processor family extended ordinary PC chips to 64 bits while still running old software, reshaping servers and desktops.

beats.title: Roadrunner Hits a Petaflop
beats.description: A supercomputer at a New Mexico lab became the first to perform a quadrillion calculations every second.

beats.title: IBM Watson Wins at Jeopardy
beats.description: A question-answering supercomputer defeated two champions on a TV quiz show, showing machines could handle natural language.

beats.title: Raspberry Pi Goes on Sale
beats.description: A credit-card-sized computer costing about the price of a meal was sold to get children and hobbyists tinkering.

beats.title: Google Unveils the TPU Chip
beats.description: Google revealed a custom processor built only for machine learning, already running in its data centres for some time.

beats.title: Google Claims Quantum Supremacy
beats.description: A superconducting chip called Sycamore reportedly solved in minutes a task that would take classical supercomputers millennia.

beats.title: Apple Unveils the M1 Chip
beats.description: Apple moved its Macs off Intel processors onto its own chip design, combining speed with remarkable battery life.

beats.title: Frontier Reaches Exascale
beats.description: A supercomputer at a US national lab became the first officially measured to perform a quintillion calculations a second.
beats.note: debuted atop the Top500 in June 2022

beats.title: Google Unveils Willow Quantum Chip
beats.description: A 105-qubit processor showed errors falling as more qubits were added, a long-sought step toward practical quantum computers.
